# ciri

> ciri is a GPU-accelerated terminal multiplexer written in Rust, with a client-server architecture similar to tmux/zellij. It supports Wayland/X11 (Linux), macOS (Metal), and Windows (DirectX 11). Rendering uses Vulkan/Metal/OpenGL via blade-graphics. Terminal emulation is based on alacritty_terminal with extensions for Kitty keyboard protocol, Sixel/Kitty graphics, and shell integration (OSC 133).

- Rust edition 2024, requires rustc 1.82+
- 13-crate workspace: ciri (client), ciri-server (daemon), ciri-app, ciri-render, ciri-gpu, ciri-term, ciri-protocol, ciri-config, ciri-input, ciri-layout, ciri-anim, ciri-session, ciri-procinfo
- Uses patched forks of winit, alacritty_terminal, and vte (branch: ciri-patches)
- Config: TOML at ~/.config/ciri/config.toml, interactive setup via `ciri init`
- Shell integration: fish and zsh via OSC 133 + OSC 7

## Key Source Files

- [Main Entry](crates/ciri/src/main.rs): Client binary entry point
- [Server Entry](crates/ciri-server/src/main.rs): Server daemon entry point
- [Key Encoding](crates/ciri/src/app/key_encode/mod.rs): Kitty keyboard protocol + legacy VT encoding
- [Protocol Messages](crates/ciri-protocol/src/message.rs): Client-server protocol definitions
- [Terminal Pane](crates/ciri-term/src/pane/mod.rs): PTY management, escape sequence handling, mode tracking
